t:
A junction diode and resistor are connected together between terminals P and Q in a box. This combination is connected to a battery of voltage 2 V and a milliammeter as shown in Fig. 20.56. The current in the circuit is 40 mA. When the terminals of the battery are interchanged, the current drops to 20 mA. The resistances of the diode and resistor are
[[img:6cd24e2f50c0]]
s:
Since the current decreases on interchanging the battery terminals, it is clear that the diode is forward biased in the first case and reverse biased in the second case. Furthermore, since the current does not drop to zero, it follows that the diode and the resistor are not connected in series because then the current should drop to zero. So they must be connected in parallel as shown in Fig. (a) and (b).
Let R_d be the resistance of the diode. In case (a) the diode is forward biased. Hence the current I₁ divides between R_d and R. The resistance of the parallel combination is
Rₚ=(2 V)/(40×10⁻³ A)=50Ω
In case (b), the diode is reverse biased and hence no current flow through it; all the current I₂ flows through R. The value of R is
R=(2 V)/(20×10⁻³ A)=100Ω
Now 1/Rₚ=1/R+1/R_d
⇒ 1/R_d=1/Rₚ−1/R=1/50−1/100⇒R_d=100Ω
So the correct choice is (a).
[[img:0b70b7e8d2ff]]

t: What will be the input of A and B for the Boolean expression bar((A+B)+(A⋅B))=1
s:
Given: bar((A+B)+(A⋅B))=1
Simplify X=(A+B)+(A⋅B):
X=A+B(1+A)=A+B(1)=A+B
Substituting back:
bar(A+B)=1
bar(A+B) is a NOR operation, which outputs 1 only when both inputs are 0.
Checking options:
A=0, B=0: bar(0+0)=0̅=1 → correct.
A=0, B=1: bar(0+1)=1̅=0 → incorrect.
A=1, B=0: bar(1+0)=1̅=0 → incorrect.
A=1, B=1: bar(1+1)=1̅=0 → incorrect.
Correct input combination: A=0, B=0. Option (1). .

⇒β=7.9/0.1=79
Hence, the required answer is α=0.99 and β=79.
